_the_rule_and_where_its_premise_failed: Describe what THAT camera can see and omit what it cannot (E02/E08). E04-twin-prompts.json used ONE constant string on all eight of the ship's views, and its stated reason was 'this subject has no view-specific ANATOMY words at all - all twelve fixture elements are material terms'. TRUE OF THE SHIP, FALSE HERE: six of the beast's eleven elements name head anatomy (D4 horns, D5 crown and cheek spikes, D8 eyes, D9 tongue, D10 fangs and tooth rows, D11 mouth interior). E12 Ruling 9d rules the per-view form for this subject: an element whose surface a view cannot see is dropped from that view's stem, because a term present in a view's prompt is an instruction to paint it and the text wins against the control (the W3 beard mechanism).
_HOW_THE_SPLIT_WAS_VERIFIED_and_where_it: Ruling 9d's default was 'D8/D9/D10/D11 drop from the rear-family views; D4 horns and D5 crown spikes stay EVERYWHERE (silhouette-visible from behind)'. Verified against all eight profile-rendered clay views with the head box drawn on each (HEADBOX_8.png) plus per-view first-hit measurement (e12_view_visibility.py). ONE DEVIATION, measured: at views 3 and 5 the head is not visible AT ALL - the near wing membrane occludes the entire skull, and the little first-hit surface falling inside the head box (0.81% of figure, against 5.35-12.79% on the head-bearing views) is WING passing through that region of space - exactly the 'a box is a region of space, not a segmentation' caveat Gate 0 attached to it. So D4 and D5 drop at 3 and 5 as well. The default's rationale HOLDS at view 4, the true rear view, where the horns and the crown/cheek frill are plainly visible from behind and nothing of the mouth or eyes is. Net: the mouth family drops at {3,4,5}; the horn family drops at {3,5}. The ivory colour family is still carried at 3 and 5 by D6 (dorsal and tail spines) and D7 (claws), both verified visible on every view.

_FINDING_the_free_standing_fang_shells_a: Measured this session, and it refines what D10 and S-filament say. The designated mesh's eight satellite shells (raw glb: 180/106/44/32/22/4/4/4 faces = 396, reproducing Gate 0's census exactly) are NOT free-standing surface: fired inward from just outside each shell along 26 directions, every direction on 7 of the 8 shells hits the MAIN shell first - only one 4-face fragment is reachable, from a single direction. Along the view-2 camera ray the crossing order through the largest fang is main -> FANG -> FANG -> main. Consistent with that, the satellites are 0 first-hit pixels on ALL EIGHT eye-level cameras. Confirmed on the raw glb as well as prep_uv.glb, so it is not a prep artifact. CONSEQUENCE, flagged not ruled: D10's VISIBLE geometry is the main-shell tooth rows, plainly visible at views 0/1/2/6/7 - the element lands, but DRAGON-IDENTITY's 'the free-standing fang shells are geometry; this element colours them' attributes it to shells no camera can reach. And S-filament's pre-registered 'losing a fang matters and goes to a ruling' would halt on geometry with no visible consequence at any gate, while cull_unseen would remove it by construction. The advisor's to re-read.
